title: Undertow: Fishing Horror Sound Effects
shortText: 112 fishing horror SFX: the wrong bite, the line that pulls back, the reveal from odd to abyssal. 20 loops. WAV + OGG.
html:
Fishing at night, when something is down there

112 fishing horror sound effects in WAV and OGG for any game engine (Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and HTML5): the fishing loop scored for dread. The cast into the dark, the wrong bite, a line that pulls back at four strengths, the line run, the snap into the deep and the slack that suddenly is not; a catch reveal from ordinary to odd to aberrant to abyssal; the boat at night (oars, an outboard that starts, idles, cuts and dies, a knock on the hull from far off to directly beneath, the anchor chain, a lantern, a fog horn, a fish finder); and what is in the water. 4 events on 5 dread waters (black lake, fog sea, ice hole at night, black swamp, open water over a trench), 20 seamless loops and a dread system in three stacking tiers. Royalty free for commercial games, no credit required. A free demo of 18 sounds is on this page.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 18 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The catch reveal at all four levels of wrongness, the wrong bite on all 5 waters, a knock on the hull from far off to directly beneath, the lantern lit, burning, guttering out and its glass cracking, and the black lake as a seamless bed.

The fishing pack, taken into the dark

This pack extends Slackwater: Fishing Sound Effects, the calm fishing loop on five waters, into a horror game, in the same grammar: one rig, placed on a water, and the relations a fishing game asks for made measurable. Here the water is a black lake that answers from a far shore, a fog sea with a swell under everything, an ice hole whose well of ice rings, a black swamp that swallows every sound, and open water over a trench, the darkest and longest of the five.

Built for the way a fishing horror game fires sounds

  • Four events, five waters: the lure landing, the wrong bite, a breach beside the boat and the float pulled under, on every

water, every pair of cells measured apart.

  • Ladders: the line pulled back at four strengths (each its own loop length, so a game crossfades as the tension climbs), the

catch reveal by wrongness, a knock on the hull by distance, and the fish finder return by size, from a small fish to something impossibly large.

  • Something is down there: three loops of one length that stack. The night on the water, then something under the boat, then

it is circling.

70 grid pairs and 12 ladder steps measured from the shipped files, failing: 0. The dread stack summed and checked again at all 3 levels.

Whole lifecycles

  • Reel: start, move (loop), stop, fail
  • Outboard motor: start, move (loop), stop, fail
  • Anchor chain: start, move (loop), stop, fail
  • Lantern: start, move (loop), stop, fail

No two states of one mechanism are the same sound renamed (24 pairs measured from the shipped files, 0 alike).

Everything in the box

  • 22 rig sounds: the cast into the dark, a heavy hook set, the rod straining and snapping, the reel engaged, winding under load and with nothing on the line, locked and seizing, the line pulled back at four strengths, the line running, snapping into the deep, and going slack before it jerks.
  • 20 events on the water: the lure landing, the wrong bite, a breach beside the boat and the float pulled under, on each of 5 waters.
  • 14 catch sounds: the reveal from ordinary to abyssal, something hauled over the gunwale, something on the deck that should not move like that, a catch slipping back into the water and a net too heavy to lift.
  • 36 boat sounds: oar strokes, oarlocks and a rowing loop, the outboard's whole life plus failed pulls and a running loop, the hull knocked, scraped from below and creaking, the anchor chain's whole life, the lantern's whole life, a fog horn near and far, and the fish finder.
  • 12 sounds from what is in the water: something circling, bubbles rising, a tail slapping the hull, something submerging, splashes far off in the dark, something dragging itself along the side, and a deep shift far below.
  • 8 beds: the five waters as seamless loops and the dread in three tiers.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by group.
  • 20 seamless loops with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • 22 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 1.34 dB, so a reel click and an abyssal reveal share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 1040 checks, 0 failed.

Already own Slackwater?

Every file here was measured against every file in Slackwater and the studio's 5 nearest packs (horror atmospheres, the underwater dive, ropes and rigging at sea, wet footsteps, creature bodies: 84224 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 84224 of 84224 are separate sounds. No file here is one of theirs at another pitch. The proof ships in the download as cross_pack_proof.json.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds designed for games, not field recordings: bubbles that ring at the pitch real bubbles ring at, wooden planks and an oak gunwale, a reel's pawl and gears, a fibreglass rod, iron chain, tin and glass, lake ice and a small outboard. There are no voices: no roars, growls, calls or screams, and no frogs, birds or insects in the beds; what is in the water is heard through the water, the hull and the line. There is no music: the fog horn and the fish finder ping are one pitch each, and no reveal carries a tune. The calm fishing loop itself is in Slackwater, not here. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover is an AI generated illustration, and the store plates are drawn by AI written code from the pack's own waveforms.

More from the same studio

  • Slackwater: Fishing Sound Effects, the calm fishing loop: cast, bite, fight and the catch on five waters.
  • Dread: Horror Sound Effects, horror atmospheres and stingers for the rest of the game.
  • Sounding: Underwater and Deep Sea Sound Effects, for when the player goes into the water.
  • Leeward: Ships, Sea and Harbour, bigger boats, rigging and the harbour.
  • Wade: Liquid, Wet and Submerged Movement, footsteps through shallows, mud and water.
